gen-gf-gabarito-gf-fahkwang: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, every stroke cut to one width. Fahkwang, the sans underneath, adds a faint pressure shift in its round letters, so extended reading feels soft and steady rather than mechanical.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-finlandica: Gabarito's open-cut terminals let its counters flow outward. Finlandica follows in a plain sans outline you could trace with a finger, its e crossbars opening up, which keeps the headline's personality from crowding the text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-fustat: Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Fustat then adds lines like bent tubing and a wide gap where the c ends, giving the sans a modern, friendly steadiness.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-gantari: Gantari has a wire-bent look across every word. Gabarito is the showier one, with one-nib strokes and open-cut terminals, while Gantari does the quiet work of wide, friendly c shapes.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-google-sans: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward and fill the line. Google Sans keeps thick-thin shifts out of its strokes, so text stays quiet beneath it.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-gruppo: Gruppo keeps its curve endings far from one another, a light, professional sans-serif touch. And Gabarito, with its tubelike lines of constant weight, takes the loud part while Gruppo handles the quieter text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-imprima: Imprima draws each line like smooth tubing, with terminals that flare outward and a neutral, approachable manner. Beneath Gabarito's one-nib heading, that sans reads smoothly down the page.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-jost: Loose, open, a little playful. Gabarito leads with one-nib strokes and cut-open terminals, while Jost keeps broad terminal gaps and a unit-width stroke, so give the Jost text a little extra size.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-koho: KoHo keeps wide c apertures and a neutral, clean manner for the text. And Gabarito, bent like neon tubing at constant thickness, supplies the showy headline energy that makes the sans feel restful.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-kosugi-maru: Kosugi Maru sets its stroke ends far apart, glowing like neon tube with one steady line thickness. Kosugi Maru and Gabarito both draw lines in a single stroke, which is the strongest link between these two sans-serif voices.
